sections.name: File setup, AuthModule
sections.title: Auth module wiring and global guards
sections.what: Registers the auth controller and its services, sets up token signing with a 15 minute default, and applies the token and roles guards to every route in the app.
sections.why: Likely reason: the comment says the guards apply to all routes, so new routes are protected by default.
sections.watch_out: Because the guards are global, any new route is locked until it is explicitly marked public.

summary: Bundles the login, token, password, social sign-in, one-time code, and MFA pieces into one module, and applies token checks to every route in the app.
purpose: Makes the auth features available and protects all routes by default.
why: Likely reason: the comment says the guards apply to all routes, so new endpoints are protected unless marked public.
how: 1. Sets up the JWT library with the secret, a 15 minute default lifetime, an issuer name, and an audience name. 2. Registers the auth controller and its services. 3. Registers the JWT and roles guards globally. 4. Exports the JWT module, token, password, and MFA services for other modules.
inputs: Settings JWT_SECRET and JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRY, read through the config service.
outputs: A registered auth module with global guards and shared services for other modules.
risks: If JWT_SECRET is missing, token signing fails. Global guards block every new route unless it is marked public. The main file checks the secret length outside development, not this file.
debug: If every route returns 401, check the guard setup and public markers. If tokens are rejected, compare the issuer and audience values with what the token was created with.
